Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the DPA you shared and had a couple of focused asks before we can route to procurement: primarily (1) confirmation that Redwood will adopt the EU SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum as executed attachments, and (2) a short transfer impact summary describing where backups and logs are stored and retention for KV/cache artifacts. Can you share a final redline and the evidence docs?

We'd like to run a signing sprint this week if possible — procurement prefers DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jaspreet

Subject: RE: FinSecure DPA + transfer appendix questions

Hi Jaspreet —

Appreciate the clarity. Attaching our current redlines and a concise transfer-impact summary. High-level notes:
- Redwood will execute the EU SCCs (controller-processor) and provide a UK IDTA addendum; we are proposing a short paragraph in the DPA that pins the SCC template version and references the executed PDF as Schedule A.
- Backups and observable logs are in US regions (primary us-west-2), customer KV caches are ephemeral and not retained beyond session TTL unless configured. Retention table is in the attached transfer-impact doc.

Next steps: Laura will lead legal sign-off on the redlines; Rishi will confirm the DocuSign envelope and signing order. If you confirm procurement wants DocuSign, we'll prepare the envelope by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redlines_20261201.docx; FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi | Sr. Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-12-02T08:22:00-08:00

Jaspreet —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick responses to your asks:
- We'll include the EU SCCs and a UK IDTA addendum as executed attachments; our redline pins the SCCs by date and edition to avoid ambiguity.
- Transfer impact summary: see page 2 of the attached PDF (we included a retention table and encrypted replication notes).
- We cannot accept broad data localization obligations, but are proposing a narrow operational commitment that agreed-upon regulated datasets can be restricted to a region via Private deployment — details in Section 4 of the redline.

If procurement confirms DocuSign, propose the following signing order: (1) Jaspreet (Privacy), (2) Procurement PO approver, (3) Redwood Legal (me), (4) Redwood Ops (Rishi) to acknowledge hosting/replication notes.

Irene/Team: please review redline changes highlighted in the doc before we finalize the envelope.

Regards,
Laura Bennett | Head, Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet.singh@finsecure.com>

Laura —

That approach sounds reasonable. Procurement confirms DocuSign and the signing order you proposed. A couple of clarifying asks from privacy: can you (1) add a one-paragraph transfer impact summary into the body of the DPA (not only as an attachment) and (2) confirm the fallback routing policy if Private deployment is requested but capacity is unavailable (we want to ensure a documented fallback path).

If you can add those two items, we can proceed with DocuSign routing tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jaspreet

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet.singh@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: RE: FinSecure DPA + transfer appendix questions

All —

Operational clarifications: fallback routing if Private deployment is not yet provisioned for a given customer region is to (a) route to our Dedicated US cluster with contractually agreed latency/throughput SLAs, with data residency controls applied at the tenancy level, or (b) enable a customer-managed VPC peering option for specific datasets. We'll add the fallback language into Section 4.3 of the redline.

DocuSign plan: I'll create the envelope and include the three external signers and two internal Redwood signers. We will request wet-sign for any exhibits that procurement deems necessary, but main DPA and SCCs will be e-signed.

-Rishi
Infrastructure & Ops
